lines: Progressive bilateral hand tremors over 2 years

He states the tremors are less noticeable at rest and do not interfere with his sleep.

encounters.cc: Found unresponsive after collapse, ventricular fibrillation arrest

lines: Found unresponsive after collapse, ventricular fibrillation arrest
The patient is a 69-year-old male with coronary artery disease, ischemic cardiomyopathy, and essential tremor, last evaluated for exertional chest pain and syncope.
His wife reports that he collapsed suddenly while walking to the kitchen.
She immediately called emergency services and initiated cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
On arrival, paramedics found the patient in ventricular fibrillation and delivered three shocks with an automated external defibrillator before return of spontaneous circulation was achieved.
The patient remains comatose with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 6.
- Stable Angina Pectoris due to Coronary Artery Disease (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
His past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction.
